speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I see you have multiple skin lesions; can you tell me how long they have been present and if they have changed in appearance?

Also, have you noticed any itching, pain, or bleeding from these spots?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Varicella (Chickenpox). Although the child is up-to-date on immunizations, breakthrough infection is possible, especially given the exposure to a sibling with recent chickenpox and a peer at daycare. The lesions are likely in the vesicular stage despite being described as papules initially. I will confirm the diagnosis by reviewing the lesion progression. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal skin lesions.
